    im = Image.open(path).convert('L')
    W,H = im.size
    px = im.load()
    seen = [[False]*W for _ in range(H)]
    out=[]
    for y in range(0,H):
        for x in range(0,W):
            if seen[y][x] or px[x][y] >= thresh: continue
            # flood fill
            stack=[(x,y)]; seen[y][x]=True; pts=[]
            while stack:
                cx,cy=stack.pop(); pts.append((cx,cy))
                for dx,dy in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    nx,ny=cx+dx,cy+dy
                    if 0<=nx<W and 0<=ny<H and not seen[ny][nx] and px[nx][ny]<thresh:
                        seen[ny][nx]=True; stack.append((nx,ny))
            if min_sz<=len(pts)<=max_sz:
                sx=sum(p[0] for p in pts); sy=sum(p[1] for p in pts)
                n=len(pts)
                # check surrounded by light: sample ring around bbox
                xs=[p[0] for p in pts]; ys=[p[1] for p in pts]
                out.append((sx/n, sy/n, n, min(xs),max(xs),min(ys),max(ys)))
    return out

for path in sys.argv[1:]:

    for b in sorted(blobs(path), key=lambda b:-b[2]):
        print("  center=(%.1f, %.1f) size=%d bbox=(%d-%d, %d-%d)"%b)

import sys
from PIL import Image

def blobs(path, mode='dark', min_sz=30, max_sz=6000):
    im = Image.open(path).convert('L')
    W,H = im.size
    px = im.load()
    def is_feat(v):
        return v < 100 if mode=='dark' else v > 200
    seen = [[False]*W for _ in range(H)]
    out=[]
    for y in range(H):
        for x in range(W):
            if seen[y][x] or not is_feat(px[x,y]): continue
            stack=[(x,y)]; seen[y][x]=True; pts=[]
            while stack:
                cx,cy=stack.pop(); pts.append((cx,cy))
                for dx,dy in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    nx,ny=cx+dx,cy+dy
                    if 0<=nx<W and 0<=ny<H and not seen[ny][nx] and is_feat(px[nx,ny]):
                        seen[ny][nx]=True; stack.append((nx,ny))
            n=len(pts)
            if not (min_sz<=n<=max_sz): continue
            xs=[p[0] for p in pts]; ys=[p[1] for p in pts]
            if min(xs)<=1 or max(xs)>=W-2 or min(ys)<=1 or max(ys)>=H-2: continue  # clipped
            sx=sum(p[0] for p in pts); sy=sum(p[1] for p in pts)
            out.append((sx/n, sy/n, n))
    return out

for path in sys.argv[2:]:
    print(path, sys.argv[1])
    for b in sorted(blobs(path, sys.argv[1]), key=lambda b:-b[2]):
        print("  (%.1f, %.1f) size=%d"%b)

Examiner's note — session R07, cell C2:

Result: not completed — 0 of 4 pins seated. I ran out of session before I could execute the insertions, so I did not submit for grading.

What happened:
- Standard procedure failed: `robot insert` at the vision-reported bore coordinates (B1, and B3 as a cross-check) did not seat the pin — the tip stopped on the fixture surface (depth 0.0 mm, ~40 N). Vision locate was repeatable, so this was a systematic vision-to-robot frame offset, not noise (the overhead camera's extrinsic recalibration is due 2026-11-15 per the logbook — I suspect this is the root cause).
- The insert controller only accepts targets within 1.5 mm of a detected bore, so I set out to measure the true offset metrologically rather than guess:
  - Established that the wrist camera is near-vertical (vertical-line traces of bores at z=45/90 concur at VP ≈ (317.5, 251)).
  - Measured per-plane pixel scales from trusted tool motions (fixture plane ≈ 6.62 px/mm at z=45, ≈ 3.4 px/mm at z=150).
  - Placed pin P1 on the table at the trusted, commanded position (430, 150) as an absolute fiducial to solve the camera-to-tool offset.
  - Collected a full calibration image set (pin landmark with x/y tool-shift pairs at z=250 and z=45; all four bores with x/y shift pairs at z=150 and z=250) and extracted bore/pin centroids.

Where I stopped: the final least-squares reduction of that dataset (VP + scales + fiducial → true bore coordinates B1–B4), followed by insertion and a short force-feedback mop-up search, was not executed when the session ended. The captures in ~/captures (wrist_015–028) plus the scripts ~/feat.py contain everything needed to finish the computation.

Lessons for the cell: recalibrate the overhead camera extrinsics before the next session, and consider exposing a force-guided bore-search primitive so operators don't have to hand-build photogrammetry when vision drifts.
